before.title: [GO, UP, MX] Live Preview of Content in CMS

after.description: AS a Content Author, I WANT to preview draft entries in CMS, SO THAT I can see how content will be shown on the website. This requires integrating the Contentstack Live Preview SDK with the existing Stack configuration and query pipeline so that draft/unpublished entries are fetched and rendered when preview mode is active. Limitation: protected pages and content may not be previewable.
after.title: [GO, UP, MX] Live Preview of Content in CMS
verificationCriteria: Given the Contentstack client is mocked, when the live preview SDK is initialized with the Stack, then the options object passed to contentstack.Stack() includes a live_preview configuration key

Given the Contentstack client is mocked to return draft entry data, when a request arrives with preview-related query parameters (e.g., live_preview=true or a contentstack preview token), then the rendered page displays the draft entry content rather than the published entry content

Given the Contentstack client is mocked, when a request arrives WITHOUT preview-related query parameters, then the rendered page displays the same published content it displayed before this change — no visual or data regression

Given the Contentstack client is mocked, when a protected page is accessed in preview mode, then the page either renders the published version or shows an appropriate access-restricted indication — draft content for protected pages is not surfaced

When the application starts without CONTENTSTACK_LIVE_PREVIEW or equivalent environment variable set, then the Stack initializes without live preview and all existing content fetching behaves identically to the current production behavior

notes: This is a novel capability — the codebase currently has zero live-preview support (grep for live_preview/livePreview/live-preview returns no matches). The Contentstack SDK Stack in src/services/contentstack.ts must be extended with live_preview config, and the query-building path through ContentstackFactory must forward preview/draft parameters. All 147+ components consume content via useContent → ContentstackContext, which is populated by data fetched through getEntry/getSingleEntry/findSingletonEntry, so the change propagates from the service layer upward without touching individual components.

notes: Openspec provided empty acceptanceCriteria with a helpful architectural note. I built all criteria from scratch after examining the actual codebase. Key findings that shaped the ACs: (1) The Stack is initialized in src/services/contentstack.ts with a flat options object — live_preview config must be added there. (2) ContentstackFactory has two query-creation methods (createContentTypeQuery for collections, createContentTypeEntryQuery for single entries) — both must forward preview parameters. (3) Three public fetch functions (getEntry, getSingleEntry, findSingletonEntry) all route through ContentstackFactory, so AC-7 ensures all paths are covered. (4) There is a separate Interactive Maps Stack — AC-8 ensures it is not inadvertently affected. (5) The story explicitly mentions protected pages may not be previewable — AC-5 addresses this. (6) The codebase uses contentstack ^3.15.2 which supports live_preview config natively. (7) Openspec's note about 'useContent → ContentstackContext' appears inaccurate for this codebase — no such pattern was found; data flows directly through the service-layer functions. This would not change the ACs but is worth noting for implementers.
